title: Design a class that is initialized with a value K and an initial list of numbers, and supports an add operation that inserts a new number and returns the Kth largest element among all numbers seen so far.
shortTitle: Kth Largest in a Stream: maintain a min-heap of size K
keyPoints: A min-heap of size K holds the K largest values seen so far; the root is the Kth largest.
On add, push the new value; if the heap exceeds K, poll the smallest, maintaining exactly K entries.
Each add costs O(log K) for push and possibly poll; querying the root is O(1).
Memory is bounded at O(K) regardless of how many values stream in.
The constructor feeds the initial list through the same add logic to seed the heap.
When fewer than K values have been seen, the heap holds all of them and the root is still the correct answer.
This is the canonical pattern for streaming top-K queries without storing the entire history.

s1_definition.oneliner: A size-K min-heap holds the K largest so far; each add pushes then trims to K, and the root is the Kth largest.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Min-heap of size K** – holds the K largest values encountered so far.
- **Root is the answer** – the smallest among the K largest is by definition the Kth largest overall.
- **Trim on add** – push the new value; if the heap exceeds K, poll the minimum to keep exactly K entries.
- **O(log K) per add** – one push and at most one poll, each O(log K).
- **O(K) memory** – the heap never grows beyond K, regardless of stream length.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine always knowing the fifth-largest donation received so far at the National Bank of India's charity event as donations keep arriving. You keep a shortlist of exactly the five biggest. When a new donation comes, you add it to the shortlist and, if the list grew to six, you drop the smallest. The smallest on that shortlist of five is always the fifth-largest overall.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Min-Heap of Size K=3:

  Stream: 50, 80, 20, 40, 90

  After 50:  [50]              Kth = 50
  After 80:  [50, 80]          Kth = 50
  After 20:  [20, 80, 50]      Kth = 20 (heap has 3)
  After 40:  offer 40, poll 20
             [40, 80, 50]      Kth = 40
  After 90:  offer 90, poll 40
             [50, 90, 80]      Kth = 50

  Heap always holds K=3 largest: root = Kth largest
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Kth Largest in a Stream asks you to return the Kth largest value among everything seen so far as new values arrive. The solution is a min-heap capped at size K that always holds exactly the K largest values. Its root, the smallest of those K, is by definition the Kth largest overall.

The add operation pushes the new value and, if the heap then exceeds K, polls the minimum to trim back. After that, the root is the answer in O(1). The constructor seeds the heap by feeding initial values through the same add logic. Each add is O(log K), and memory stays at O(K) regardless of stream length.

In a banking system at the National Bank of India, a fraud dashboard shows the Kth largest transaction as a live watermark. The min-heap answers each incoming transaction in logarithmic time while holding only K values, keeping the watermark current without growing memory.

This is the canonical pattern for streaming top-K queries. It avoids storing the entire history and handles unbounded streams efficiently.

Remember one sentence: a size-K min-heap holds the K largest values seen, and its root is always the Kth largest, updated in O(log K) per new element.
